name: Wenzhe Xu
headline: Hi, I’m Wenzhe Xu.
intro: I am a researcher interested in how people understand, use, and live with emerging technologies. I am good at identifying wicked design problems and creating better user-centered solutions.

My current research focuses on designing thoughtful digital systems and studying their social impact. I am especially interested in work that turns careful observation into practical, human-centred design.
Key Words: Smart Manufacturing, Industry 5.0, Inclusive Design, Cognitive Ergonomics

projects.title: Warehouse Management System (WMS) for Unifree Co.
projects.summary:
- Assembled a multidisciplinary team to investigate usage scenarios at the Hefei Unifree factory, drew user journeys map, and prioritize solutions
- Developed design guidelines based on product features of Black Lake
projects.detail: - Shortened the operation time of warehouse workers by half. Received the 2023 Best Partner Award by Unifree

projects.title: Manufacturing Execution System (MES) for A.O. Smith Co.
projects.summary: An investigation into workers’ use habits in the A.O. Smith gas water heater factory found that the MES’s terminal which is vertical mobile device mode affecting the workers’ efficiency at fixed workstations.

projects.title: E-WASTE
projects.summary:
Conducted desk research, focus groups, and field research across Paris to identify barriers to device repair,
including high costs, long wait times, uncertain repair quality, and limited access to repair information
• Designed a system with a citywide repair-shop network, service network map, device teardown information, and
digital repair guides to make repair more accessible

projects.title: From Opposites to Unity & 'Jump out of Frame'
projects.summary: Took Giacometti’s Man Pointing and copper wire (a common building material) as dual exhibits, deconstructed the single valuation and narrative authority of traditional museums.

projects.title: Temporary Autonomous Museum
projects.summary: Utilized tools such as stakeholder maps and service design blueprints and applied service design research methods, a temporary autonomous museum was constructed at the Leake Street Arches, with the aim of provoking visitors to reflect on their relationship with physical space, facilitating the artistic expression of the artists in the graffiti tunnels and driving the traffic of merchants.
